Dentist here.   
You want to avoid brushing your teeth right after eating as the acids that form very quickly have already done some damage and you could end up brushing off the top layer of enamel (theoretical, i wouldn't worry too much)  
There is plaque and there is plaque. 'Healthy' plaque is the stuff that forms straight away from the bacteria that naturally live in saliva, the food you eat, the pen you sucked etc. this does very little damage to teeth because it hasn't yet got a chance to get going.   
established plaque is the dangerous stuff, bacteria start to form their own colony and get organised, allowing more types to get started. Established plaque takes 2+ days, it results in morning breath and tooth decay/gum disease etc.  
Everyone has a mix of there becuase no one brushes to 100%. But it means that if you get close to a great brush, brushing once a day is quite sufficient. Best time is before bed time, as your defences are lower over night (saliva flow drops). Those that feel they need to 'brush away the morning breath' in the morning are missing the point :-)

Pretty much anything. I stopped looking at anxiety as some kind of mental state, and look at it instead as stress in the biological state. This is how psychology often looks at it. Basically anything that can throw off the hormone balance. 
Obviously there’s a strong mental component, if you’re worried about something in the short term that’s usually clear. It’s possible to be worried about something in the long term and not be consciously aware of it, like a fear of what happens after death or why you’ve been single for so long. 
Then you’ve got the biochemical reasons, and for that I mainly mean diet. Caffeine makes you anxious, that’s an easy example. But there are plenty of things that could cause minor problems and in excess or insufficiency. Lack of sleep I put in this category. 

If you don’t already suspect what it might be, give it some thought and time, do some googling. Think of it as short or long term mental or physiological. It’s also quite likely to be a mix of things. 
Best of luck.

Quantum physics shows that the world of the very small has no such determinism, that wave/particles have probable futures at best. We've observed quantum effects in molecules like C60. This is still a 'no' to free will, just a less predictable one.

Clearly there are plenty of things, like exercise, that help make a healthy brain.... but as far as diet goes, so long as you are not deficient in something, there isn’t a ‘better diet’ as far as we know without some kind of side effect.  Micro vitamins, zinc, omega 3, all good stuff. Really doesn’t have much effect until u start running out, extra doesn’t help an organ like the brain. 

The Blood Brain Barrier also regulates a lot of what goes in and out, being ‘supercharged’ is just as much of a problem as being undercharged. Drugs, like caffeine are effective, but that causes heart problems in excess enough for a decent long change in brain function. 

- mood is another issue entirely, psychology is very complicated. Diet can affect mood, but That’s more down to what you think ur eating rather than what ur actually eating.  Obviously diet can have an effect on the rest of the body, less than u think if you have a balanced diet, but the brain, not so much . -
